H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper organizes control by physical tanks and flat modes such as off/ready/reserve-low/reserve-full; it does not define nested or composite states.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Multiple sensor guards drive behavior: I3 on/off, I1 reserve minimum, I6 reserve upper, I2 operation-tank full, I5 below desired level, and I4 user-tank overflow.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Actions are actuator commands: stop the pump motor, open/close solenoid valves Q2/Q3/Q5, and result steps such as 'When I1 ON Q4 and Q5 is ON however motor Q1 is OFF'.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The reserve tank has dry-run protection: if liquid is finished, 'the motor operation to stop'; overflow sensors close valves, but no layered fault hierarchy is specified.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: I/O names are introduced in the block diagram, detailed tank rules appear in Section 3.2.2-3.2.4, and output combinations are later enumerated in Result & Simulation.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: The paper uses domain terms such as 'dry run' and says a manual start/stop switch will 'totally override the automatic system', requiring priority semantics beyond a simple event name.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are embedded in prose, e.g. the operation-tank full sensor makes the PLC 'close the solenoid valve Q2' and the lower sensor makes it 'open Q2'.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The actual control rules are mostly single-sensor threshold/on-off guards; no clear arithmetic or substantial multi-variable boolean guard is specified.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No parent/composite state with its own entry/during/exit behavior is described.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: The main switch and manual override are global: 'When I3 is off all the system off' and the manual start/stop switch 'will totally override the automatic system'.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is no composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The guards are simple sensor thresholds/on-off conditions, not arithmetic-plus-boolean constraints suitable for SMT consistency checking.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: The global off/manual override rule applies across the controller's tank-control conditions and could be encoded once as a forced transition instead of duplicated.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs are concrete PLC actuator commands to pumps, solenoid valves, and an indicator, not abstract log/publish/notify actions.

key_nl_quotes: When the system switch I3 is ON the overall system is ready ... if I3 is off ... the overall operation is off mode.
In this tanker there is a low level control system which controls the dry run implies that, if the water (liquid) is finished the motor operation to stop.
one_line_pitch: A modest but useful PLC stress case where simple tank-level guards map to multiple actuator outputs, dry-run protection, and a global manual/off override split across the paper.
rationale: This sample has meaningful guard/action/fault content, especially multiple level sensors mapped to pump and valve commands plus dry-run protection. It is weak on hierarchy and has mostly simple threshold guards, so it is not a top stress-test candidate for composite-state modeling. Its main benchmark value is baseline-trap density: the required state-machine semantics are scattered across block diagram text, tank descriptions, and result steps, with a global override/off rule.
